data.name: Plan.RoutineText
data.value: The same steps every night, 20 to 30 minutes: a wash or bath, pyjamas and a fresh diaper, a feed, a song or a book, then into the cot. Dim lights and quiet voices in the last hour; daylight soon after waking in the morning. Now and then, put {0} down drowsy but awake, to practise falling asleep in the cot.

data.name: Plan.SafeSleep
data.value: Safe sleep, always: on the back, on a firm flat surface, nothing loose in the cot, in your room for the first 6 months.

data.name: Plan.StopConfirm
data.value: Stop this plan? It stays in the past plans.

data.name: Plan.Text.Chair
data.value: After the routine, sit on a chair next to the cot until {0} falls asleep; comfort with your voice and a hand, and pick up only when needed. Every 3 nights move the chair further away: halfway to the door, at the door, then just outside. Answer night wakings the same way as bedtime.

data.name: Plan.Text.CheckAndConsole
data.value: After the routine, put {0} down awake and leave the room. If {0} cries, go back after a few minutes, comfort briefly with your voice and a hand without picking up, and leave again. You choose the intervals; many parents start at 3 minutes and make them a little longer over the nights. Always go in for anything that sounds like pain or illness, or for a dirty diaper.

data.name: Plan.Text.Fading
data.value: Settle {0} the way you do now, then use a little less help every 2 to 3 nights: rocking becomes holding still, holding becomes patting in the cot, patting becomes a hand resting on {0}, then sitting nearby. If {0} gets very upset, go one step back for a night. You stay in the room until {0} is asleep.

data.name: Plan.Text.NoCrying
data.value: {0} is never left to cry: you comfort every time. The plan works through timing (the right wake windows, an earlier bedtime when overtired) and the routine, with very small steps of less help, as in fading. Progress is slower than with other approaches, often weeks rather than days. That is expected.

data.name: Plan.Text.Rhythm
data.value: Keep to the planned times and the routine, and settle {0} the way that works for you now: rocking, feeding or holding to sleep is fine. Start winding down a little before each planned nap; yawning, staring or rubbing eyes means it is time. Days bright and lively, nights dark and quiet; night feeds calm and short.
